subject: histology
prompt: A patient can feel sustained pressure but cannot detect a pinprick, an excessively hot surface, or histamine-induced itching in a patch of skin. Which receptor type is most directly impaired?
explanation: Free nerve endings extend through the papillary dermis into lower epidermal layers and are the principal cutaneous receptors for pain, temperature extremes, and itching. They can also contribute to crude touch.

distractorExplanations.B: Merkel complexes are tonic mechanoreceptors for sustained light touch and texture, not the principal receptors for pain, temperature, and itch.
distractorExplanations.C: Meissner corpuscles are encapsulated phasic receptors for light touch and low-frequency deformation.
distractorExplanations.D: Pacinian corpuscles are deep encapsulated receptors for coarse pressure and high-frequency vibration.

learningObjective: Associate free nerve endings with pain, temperature, itching, and crude tactile input.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Epidermal free nerve endings detect pain, temperature extremes, itching, and mechanical movements of the skin.

subject: histology
prompt: Which receptor-location-function combination best identifies the tonic receptor that continues signaling while a small object presses against the skin?

options.text: Merkel cell-neurite complex in the stratum basale; sustained light touch and texture
Meissner corpuscle in the hypodermis; high-frequency vibration
Pacinian corpuscle in the epidermis; pain and temperature
Root hair plexus in glabrous skin; sustained deep pressure

acceptedFreeText: Merkel cell-neurite complex in the stratum basale; sustained light touch and texture
explanation: Merkel cells lie in the basal epidermis and contact expanded sensory axon endings. Their tonic response preserves information about sustained light touch and surface texture.

distractorExplanations.B: Meissner corpuscles lie in dermal papillae and respond rapidly to light touch or low-frequency deformation.
distractorExplanations.C: Pacinian corpuscles are deep in reticular dermis or hypodermis and detect pressure and high-frequency vibration.
distractorExplanations.D: Root hair plexuses surround hair follicles in hairy skin and respond to hair movement.

learningObjective: Identify Merkel complexes by their basal epidermal location and tonic texture-sensing function.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Merkel cells with expanded axonal endings are tonic receptors for sustained light touch and object texture.

subject: histology
prompt: A small elliptical encapsulated receptor located inside a dermal papilla of a fingertip is most specialized for which sensory input?

options.text: Light touch and low-frequency skin deformation

acceptedFreeText: Light touch and low-frequency skin deformation
explanation: Meissner corpuscles occupy dermal papillae, especially in fingertips, palms, and soles. They are rapidly responding encapsulated mechanoreceptors for light touch and low-frequency deformation.

distractorExplanations.B: Ruffini corpuscles detect stretch, tension, and twisting of tissue.
distractorExplanations.C: Pacinian corpuscles detect high-frequency vibration and deeper pressure.
distractorExplanations.D: Free nerve endings are the main receptors for pain, temperature extremes, and itch.

learningObjective: Match Meissner corpuscles with dermal papillae, glabrous skin, and light-touch input.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Meissner corpuscles in dermal papillae detect light touch and low-frequency stimuli and are numerous in fingertips, palms, and soles.

subject: histology
prompt: Which receptor is preferentially activated by a high-frequency vibrating instrument pressed firmly against the skin?
explanation: Pacinian corpuscles are large, deeply located, rapidly adapting mechanoreceptors whose concentric lamellae transmit changes in coarse pressure and high-frequency vibration to the central axon.

distractorExplanations.A: Merkel complexes encode sustained light touch and texture in the basal epidermis.
distractorExplanations.B: Root hair plexuses detect displacement of hairs rather than deep high-frequency vibration.
distractorExplanations.D: Free nerve endings mainly signal pain, temperature, itch, and some crude touch.

learningObjective: Associate Pacinian corpuscles with deep pressure and high-frequency vibration.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Lamellated Pacinian corpuscles detect coarse touch, pressure, and high-frequency vibration.

subject: histology
prompt: A small ovoid encapsulated receptor in the skin of the glans penis or clitoris is described in Junqueira as responding primarily to what?
explanation: Krause end bulbs are simple encapsulated ovoid receptors found mainly in genital skin and are described as sensing low-frequency vibration or movement.

distractorExplanations.B: High-frequency vibration and deep pressure are characteristic of Pacinian corpuscles.
distractorExplanations.C: Sustained texture discrimination is characteristic of Merkel cell-neurite complexes.
distractorExplanations.D: Noxious temperature and itch are detected mainly by free nerve endings.

learningObjective: Recognize the location and tested modality of Krause end bulbs.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Krause end bulbs are found primarily in penile and clitoral skin and sense low-frequency vibrations.

subject: histology
prompt: A fusiform encapsulated receptor is firmly anchored to surrounding dermal connective tissue. Deformation of its collagenous capsule most directly signals which stimulus?

options.text: Fine low-force texture at the basal epidermis

explanation: Ruffini corpuscles have fusiform collagenous capsules anchored to connective tissue. Stretch or torque distorts the capsule and stimulates the sensory axon.

distractorExplanations.B: Hair movement is detected by a root hair plexus.
distractorExplanations.C: Pain is detected mainly by free nerve endings.
distractorExplanations.D: Sustained light touch and texture at the basal epidermis are detected by Merkel complexes.

learningObjective: Associate Ruffini corpuscles with tissue stretch, tension, and torque.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Ruffini corpuscles have fusiform collagenous capsules and detect tissue distortion, stretch, or twisting.

subject: histology
prompt: A slight breeze bends hairs on the forearm without appreciably indenting the skin. Which receptor transduces this movement most directly?
explanation: The root hair plexus is an unencapsulated web of sensory fibers around the base of a hair follicle in the reticular dermis. Bending the hair deforms these endings and produces a light-touch signal.

distractorExplanations.B: Pacinian corpuscles respond to deeper pressure and high-frequency vibration.
distractorExplanations.C: Merkel complexes respond tonically to direct sustained touch and texture.
distractorExplanations.D: Krause end bulbs are encapsulated genital receptors for low-frequency vibration.

learningObjective: Identify root hair plexuses as receptors for hair displacement in hairy skin.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Root hair plexuses surround hair-follicle bases in the reticular dermis and detect hair movement.

subject: histology
prompt: A histology section shows a 100-micrometer elliptical structure within a dermal papilla. Flattened modified Schwann cells form stacked transverse layers around winding sensory axons. What is it?
explanation: The superficial dermal-papilla location and stacked flattened Schwann cells oriented roughly perpendicular to the epidermis are the classic recognition clues for a Meissner tactile corpuscle.

distractorExplanations.B: A Pacinian corpuscle is much larger, deep, and onion-like with many concentric lamellae.
distractorExplanations.C: A Ruffini corpuscle is fusiform with a collagenous capsule anchored to surrounding tissue.
distractorExplanations.D: A root hair plexus is an unencapsulated web around a hair follicle rather than an oval corpuscle in a dermal papilla.

learningObjective: Recognize Meissner corpuscles by microscopic architecture and superficial location.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Meissner corpuscles are elliptical structures in dermal papillae containing axons among stacked flattened Schwann cells.

subject: histology
prompt: A large oval receptor among adipocytes in the hypodermis contains 15-50 concentric lamellae surrounding a central axon. Which structure is shown?
explanation: The deep location, large size, and onion-like concentric lamellae of modified Schwann cells are diagnostic of a Pacinian corpuscle.

distractorExplanations.A: A Merkel complex is microscopic and unencapsulated in the stratum basale.
distractorExplanations.B: A Meissner corpuscle is smaller and superficial, with stacked layers inside a dermal papilla rather than concentric onion-like lamellae.
distractorExplanations.D: A free nerve ending lacks a capsule and cannot form this large lamellated structure.

learningObjective: Recognize Pacinian corpuscles by their onion-like lamellae and deep location.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Pacinian corpuscles are large deep oval structures with 15-50 concentric lamellae around an axonal core.

subject: histology
prompt: Which group contains only unencapsulated cutaneous sensory receptors?

options.text: Free nerve endings, Merkel tactile discs, and root hair plexuses
Merkel tactile discs, Meissner corpuscles, and Krause end bulbs
Free nerve endings, Pacinian corpuscles, and root hair plexuses

acceptedFreeText: Free nerve endings, Merkel tactile discs, and root hair plexuses
explanation: Free nerve endings, Merkel-associated tactile discs, and root hair plexuses lack connective-tissue capsules. Meissner, Pacinian, Krause, and Ruffini receptors are encapsulated.

distractorExplanations.B: All three listed structures are encapsulated receptors.
distractorExplanations.C: Meissner corpuscles and Krause end bulbs are encapsulated.
distractorExplanations.D: Pacinian corpuscles possess a conspicuous multilamellar capsule.

learningObjective: Classify cutaneous receptors as encapsulated or unencapsulated.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Free endings, Merkel discs, and root hair plexuses are unencapsulated; Meissner, Pacinian, Krause, and Ruffini receptors are encapsulated.

subject: histology
prompt: A receptor continues to discharge while a textured object remains stationary against the skin, whereas another responds strongly when light contact first deforms the skin and then adapts rapidly. Which pair best matches these responses?

options.text: Merkel complex first; Meissner corpuscle second
Meissner corpuscle first; Merkel complex second
Pacinian corpuscle first; free nerve ending second
Root hair plexus first; Ruffini corpuscle second

acceptedFreeText: Merkel complex first; Meissner corpuscle second
explanation: Merkel complexes are tonic receptors that preserve information during sustained light touch. Meissner corpuscles are encapsulated phasic mechanoreceptors that respond rapidly to changing light-touch deformation.

distractorExplanations.B: This reverses the adaptation patterns: Merkel is tonic and Meissner is phasic.
distractorExplanations.C: Pacinian corpuscles are phasic high-frequency and pressure receptors, while free endings mainly signal pain, temperature, itch, and crude touch.
distractorExplanations.D: Root hair plexuses emphasize hair movement; this pair does not provide the classic tonic sustained-texture versus phasic light-touch contrast.

learningObjective: Use tonic versus phasic behavior to distinguish Merkel and Meissner receptors.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Merkel complexes are tonic receptors; encapsulated receptors such as Meissner corpuscles respond rapidly to mechanical change.

subject: histology
prompt: An age-related decline in which receptor helps explain worsening two-point discrimination at the fingertips?
explanation: Meissner corpuscles are densely represented in fingertips and support fine spatial discrimination of light touch. Junqueira notes that their density declines during adult life and can be estimated by two-point discrimination testing.

distractorExplanations.B: Pacinian corpuscles primarily detect deep pressure and high-frequency vibration, not fine superficial two-point discrimination.
distractorExplanations.C: Free nerve endings primarily mediate pain, temperature, itch, and crude tactile input.
distractorExplanations.D: Ruffini corpuscles primarily detect stretch and torque.

learningObjective: Connect fingertip two-point discrimination with Meissner corpuscle density.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: Meissner corpuscle density can be estimated by two-point discrimination and normally declines during adult life.

subject: histology
prompt: Which superficial-to-deep sequence of cutaneous receptors is correct?

options.text: Merkel complex in basal epidermis -> Meissner corpuscle in dermal papilla -> Pacinian corpuscle in deep reticular dermis or hypodermis
Pacinian corpuscle in basal epidermis -> Merkel complex in dermal papilla -> Meissner corpuscle in hypodermis
Meissner corpuscle in stratum corneum -> Pacinian corpuscle in papillary dermis -> Merkel complex in hypodermis
Ruffini corpuscle in epidermis -> free nerve ending only in hypodermis -> Merkel complex around a hair bulb

acceptedFreeText: Merkel complex in basal epidermis -> Meissner corpuscle in dermal papilla -> Pacinian corpuscle in deep reticular dermis or hypodermis
explanation: Merkel complexes are epidermal, Meissner corpuscles occupy superficial dermal papillae, and the large Pacinian corpuscles lie deep in reticular dermis or subcutaneous tissue.

distractorExplanations.B: All three structures are assigned to the wrong depths.
distractorExplanations.C: Meissner corpuscles are not in the stratum corneum, and Merkel complexes are not hypodermal.
distractorExplanations.D: Ruffini corpuscles are encapsulated dermal receptors; free endings extend into superficial skin; Merkel cells occupy the basal epidermis.

learningObjective: Map the principal cutaneous mechanoreceptors from epidermis to hypodermis.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: The receptor map places Merkel discs in basal epidermis, Meissner corpuscles in dermal papillae, and Pacinian corpuscles deep in dermis or hypodermis.

subject: histology
prompt: Which two sensory structures may extend into or reside within the epidermis rather than forming encapsulated corpuscles in the dermis?

options.text: Free nerve endings and Merkel-associated tactile discs
Ruffini corpuscles and Krause end bulbs
Root hair plexuses and Pacinian corpuscles

acceptedFreeText: Free nerve endings and Merkel-associated tactile discs
explanation: Free sensory endings can extend into lower epidermal layers, and Merkel cells with their tactile discs lie in the stratum basale. Both are unencapsulated.

distractorExplanations.B: Meissner and Pacinian corpuscles are encapsulated and lie in dermis or hypodermis.
distractorExplanations.C: Ruffini corpuscles and Krause end bulbs are encapsulated dermal receptors.
distractorExplanations.D: Root hair plexuses surround follicles in the reticular dermis, while Pacinian corpuscles lie deep.

learningObjective: Identify the principal sensory structures associated with the epidermis.

source.title: Junqueira's Basic Histology
source.excerpt: The epidermis contains free nerve endings and Merkel-associated tactile discs, both with unencapsulated nerve fibers.
